questions.question: The Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) has notified new rules for the cancellation of the registration of Overseas Citizens of India in August 2025. Under which Act have these rules been issued?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Citizenship Act, 1955**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA)** notified the new rules in **August 2025** to streamline the process of **registration** and **cancellation** of the **Overseas Citizen of India (OCI)** status.
 
• These rules were issued under the **Citizenship Act, 1955**, which is the primary legislation governing the acquisition, determination, and termination of **Indian citizenship** and **OCI** status.
 
• Under **Section 7D** of the **Citizenship Act, 1955**, the **Central Government** holds the authority to cancel the **OCI registration** if the person has shown disaffection towards the **Constitution of India** or violated any laws notified by the government.
 
• The **2025 notification** emphasizes that any **OCI cardholder** found involved in activities prejudicial to the **sovereignty, integrity, and security** of **India** will face immediate **cancellation** of their status.
 
• The **OCI card** is a multipurpose document that allows foreign citizens of Indian origin to live and work in **India** indefinitely, but it does not confer **voting rights** or the right to hold **public office**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Citizenship Act, 1955:**

 
 
• This **Act** provides for the acquisition of citizenship by **birth, descent, registration, naturalization**, and **incorporation of territory**.
 
• It has been amended several times, most notably in **1986, 1992, 2003, 2005, 2015, and 2019**.
 
• The **OCI scheme** was introduced by the **Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2005** in response to demands for dual citizenship by the **Indian diaspora**.
 
 
 
• **Passport Act, 1967:**
 
 
• This **Act** regulates the issuance of **passports** and travel documents to **Indian citizens**.
 
• While it governs travel, it does not deal with the **registration** or **cancellation** of **OCI** status. ***Hence, option 1 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Foreigners Act, 1946:**
 
 
• This **Act** empowers the **Indian government** to regulate the **entry, stay, and departure** of **foreign nationals** in **India**.
 
• Although **OCI holders** are foreign nationals, their specific **registration** rights are governed by the **Citizenship Act** rather than this general act. ***Hence, option 2 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Indian Penal Code, 1860:**
 
 
• This was the official **criminal code** of **India** (now replaced by **Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita** in recent reforms).
 
• It defines **offenses** and provides **punishments** but does not contain provisions for **citizenship** or **OCI registration**. ***Hence, option 3 is incorrect.***
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Rights of OCI Cardholders:**
 
• They enjoy **parity with Non-Resident Indians (NRIs)** in economic, financial, and educational fields, except in the acquisition of **agricultural or plantation properties**.
 
• **Grounds for Cancellation:**
 
• Registration can be cancelled if it was obtained through **fraud**, false representation, or if the **OCI holder** is sentenced to **imprisonment** for not less than **two years** within **five years** of registration.
 
• **The 2019 Amendment:**
 
• The **Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2019** significantly expanded the **Central Government's** power to cancel **OCI status** if the holder violates any **local law** as specified by the **MHA**.
 
• **Designation:** The **Ministry of Home Affairs** is the nodal ministry for all matters relating to **citizenship** and **foreigners' registration** in **India**.

questions.question: In July 2025, the Defence Research and Development Organisation successfully conducted flight tests of the Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Launched Precision Guided Missile (ULPGM)-V3 at the National Open Area Range test facility in ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kurnool, Andhra Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **July 2025**, the **Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO)** successfully conducted the flight tests of the **Unmanned Launch Precision Guided Missile (ULPGM)-V3**.
 
• The testing took place at the **National Open Area Range (NOAR)**, which is located in **Kurnool, Andhra Pradesh**.
 
• The **ULPGM-V3** is a sophisticated air-to-surface missile specifically designed to be launched from **Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs)** to engage ground targets with high accuracy.
 
• During the flight tests, the missile's **precision guidance system**, **aerodynamic stability**, and **warhead triggering mechanism** were evaluated under realistic combat scenarios.
 
• This successful trial represents a significant step toward indigenous **precision-strike capabilities** and reduces dependency on foreign weapon systems for India's growing drone fleet.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **DRDO (Defence Research and Development Organisation):**

 
 
• It was established in **1958** and functions under the **Ministry of Defence**, Government of India.
 
• Headquartered in **New Delhi**, its primary mission is to achieve self-reliance in critical defense technologies and systems.
 
• It operates a network of more than **50 laboratories** across the country developing various technologies like aeronautics, armaments, electronics, and missiles.
 
 
 
• **National Open Area Range (NOAR), Kurnool:**
 
 
• Located in the **Orvakal** region of **Kurnool district**, this facility provides a vast, unobstructed area for testing various missile and rocket systems.
 
• It complements other major testing sites like the **Integrated Test Range (ITR)** at **Chandipur, Odisha**.
 
• The **Andhra Pradesh** government has been actively supporting the development of defense corridors and specialized testing ranges within the state.
 
 
 
• **Unmanned Launch Precision Guided Missiles (ULPGM):**
 
 
• These are "smart" munitions that utilize **laser guidance**, **GPS**, or **Inertial Navigation Systems (INS)** to strike targets with minimal collateral damage.
 
• The integration of such missiles with indigenous UAVs like the **TAPAS-BH-201** or **Archer** enhances the tactical offensive reach of the **Indian Armed Forces**.
 
• The **V3 variant** indicates an advanced iteration with improved range, seeker technology, and weight-to-payload ratio.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Strategic Significance:** The development of the **ULPGM-V3** aligns with the **Atmanirbhar Bharat** (Self-Reliant India) initiative in the defense sector.
 
• **Recent Trends:** Modern warfare is increasingly shifting toward **Unmanned Combat Aerial Vehicles (UCAVs)**, making specialized miniature precision munitions a critical requirement for **21st-century** defense strategy.
 
• **Geographic Location:** **Kurnool** is strategically chosen for its topography and lower population density, ensuring safety during high-velocity **missile flight trials**.

questions.question: The Parliament of India passed the Immigration and Foreigners Bill in April ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2025**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Indian Parliament** successfully passed the **Immigration and Foreign Subjects Bill** in **April 2025** to modernize the nation's legal framework regarding international travel and residency.
 
• The primary objective of this bill is to consolidate and replace aging statutes, such as the **Foreigners Act, 1946**, ensuring that the regulation of **foreign nationals** aligns with contemporary **national security** requirements.
 
• The **2025** legislation introduces a comprehensive **digital tracking system** for all foreign subjects, requiring mandatory **biometric registration** for those staying in the **country** for more than **90 days**.
 
• It grants the **Central Government** enhanced powers to regulate the **entry, stay, and departure** of individuals, specifically targeting the prevention of **illegal immigration** and **visa overstays**.
 
• The bill also simplifies the process for **skilled professionals** and **investors**, aiming to boost the **Indian economy** by attracting global talent through a more transparent **visa regime**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Foreigners Act, 1946:**

 
 
• This was the foundational law used by the **Government of India** for decades to regulate the presence of foreigners. It gave the **Executive** broad discretionary powers to detain and **deport** individuals deemed to be in the **country** illegally.
 
 
 
• **Bureau of Immigration (BoI):**
 
 
• The **BoI** is the dedicated agency responsible for managing **Immigration Check Posts (ICPs)** at **airports**, **seaports**, and **land borders**. It functions under the **Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA)**.
 
 
 
• **e-Visa Facility:**
 
 
• India provides **e-Visas** to citizens of over **160 countries**. The new legislative changes in **2025** aim to further digitize this process, reducing the **processing time** for **Tourist**, **Business**, and **Medical visas**.
 
 
 
• **Passport (Entry into India) Act, 1920:**
 
 
• This act requires persons entering **India** to possess valid **passports**. The **Immigration and Foreign Subjects Bill, 2025** works in tandem with this act to ensure **border integrity**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **National Security:** The **2025 bill** emphasizes the use of **Artificial Intelligence (AI)** to flag suspicious **travel patterns**, thereby assisting **intelligence agencies** in maintaining internal safety.
 
• **Visa Categories:** The **legislation** clarifies the rights and restrictions associated with various categories, such as **Employment Visas**, **Student Visas**, and **Research Visas**, ensuring that **foreign subjects** comply with the specific purposes of their visit.
 
• **Legislative Authority:** Under the **Constitution of India**, matters related to **citizenship**, **naturalization**, and **aliens** fall under the **Union List**, giving the **Parliament** exclusive power to enact such laws.
 
• **Role of the President:** After being passed by both the **Lok Sabha** and the **Rajya Sabha** in **April 2025**, the bill received the **Presidential Assent**, officially turning it into an **Act of Parliament**.

• In **June 2025**, she reached a significant career milestone by winning the women's singles title at the **French Open**, one of the four prestigious **Grand Slam** tournaments.
